_README: Errors matched here are downgraded from 'error' to 'ignored'. They are NOT hidden:
every ignored event is printed in the run log under the rule that matched it, counted
in result.json counts.ignored, and listed in full in result.json 'ignored'.
A rule matches an event when EVERY key present in 'match' matches. 'text' is a regex
against the message; 'url' is a regex against the event's source URL AND against any
http(s) URL embedded in the message text (vite reports the failing module in the text,
'scope' records why the entry is defensible:
benign        - happens on a stock ComfyUI including a buyer's, and is not a defect
(an optional resource the frontend probes for unconditionally)
environment   - only happens on this pod; a buyer following the NSFW bootstrap
would not have the pack that causes it
product-known - a REAL defect in what we ship, deliberately not gating the harness
because it is cosmetic and would otherwise make every run red.
Every entry with this scope must be written up in the WS2 report.
Keep this list at zero if you can.
Disable the whole file with --no-default-ignores. Add ad-hoc rules with --ignore-error.
frontend-conversion and execution failures are never ignorable, whatever is listed here.

rules.reason: user.css is ComfyUI's optional user stylesheet override, requested unconditionally on every page load by both the static path and the userdata API. It does not ship with comfyui_frontend_package (verified: no user.css under .../comfyui_frontend_package/static/) and is absent here (verified: no /workspace/ComfyUI/user/default/user.css). Verified live: GET /user.css -> 404 and GET /api/userdata/user.css -> 404. A buyer on a clean install sees both.

comfy.templates.json holds the user's saved node templates. ComfyUI only writes it once the user saves one. Verified live: GET /api/userdata/comfy.templates.json -> 404. A buyer on a clean install sees this.

The frontend lists the user's saved subgraph-blueprint directory on boot. ComfyUI only creates it once the user saves a blueprint. Verified live: GET /api/userdata?dir=subgraphs&recurse=true&split=false&full_info=true -> 404. A buyer on a clean install sees this.

The frontend probes for an optional per-directory workflow index file. Absent here (verified: /workspace/ComfyUI/user/default/workflows/ holds only the .json workflows themselves) and verified live -> 404. Fires on any install that has never written one, including a buyer's.

CORRECTED BY THE RUN-3 FRESH INSTALL: the NSFW bootstrap DOES install ComfyUI-Custom-Scripts (the installer reuses the video NODE_REPOS wholesale), so every buyer has this route and sees this 404 once per boot until they create the optional word list. Upstream behavior, cosmetic, does not gate. The real fix is trimming NODE_REPOS to the packs the NSFW graph uses -- recorded as the top follow-up; deferred because the 'Workflow node check' stage hard-names video packs and editing install-check logic during a distribution cut risks more than labeled console noise.

CORRECTED BY THE RUN-3 FRESH INSTALL: ComfyUI_Swwan IS installed by the NSFW bootstrap (video NODE_REPOS reused wholesale), so every buyer's boot logs ~39 vite preloadError lines from its two missing web files. Upstream pack defect, cosmetic, never gates (boot phase). Real fix: drop Swwan from the NSFW NODE_REPOS -- it is a video-only rgthree fork the NSFW graph never references, and it also causes the extension-name collisions with the rgthree-comfy this graph DOES need. Same follow-up and same deferral reason as pysssss above.

CORRECTED BY THE RUN-3 FRESH INSTALL: both colliding packs (rgthree-comfy and its fork ComfyUI_Swwan) are installed by the NSFW bootstrap, so every buyer sees these collisions, not just this pod. Cosmetic; the needed rgthree features won the registration in every observed run. Fixed for real by the same NODE_REPOS trim.
